text.p: Italian bond futures slipped lower by late afternoon in line with many other global bond markets following stronger than expected U.S. housing data and some caution ahead of Italian CPI data later this week.

Dealers said that preliminary data from ten Italian cities on Thursday and Friday was likely to see CPI inflation held at November's 2.6 percent rate in December, while Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi added today he saw Italian inflation levelling out at November's 2.6 percent level.
"If inflation is steady in December it might not be enough to push the Bank of Italy into cutting rate," one trader said.
Many dealers had hoped that the CPI inflation data for December would prompt Italy's central bank into its third cut in interest rates this year.

But the biggest jolt to the market came from overseas, with construction starts on U.S. new homes and apartments jumping at the sharpest rate for 16 months during November with total starts up 9.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted 1.514 million.

This figure was far above economists' forecasts for a 1.39 million unit rise, and this together with the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting today, kept many investors on the cautious side.

Ciampi also said today at a news conference he did not think the government would have to resort to a mini-budget next year after its 62.5 trillion lire main package for 1997, but he would weigh up the situation.

Investors were also keeping their eyes of the passage of this budget bill, where the Senate is expected to approve the last items by Wednesday before the draft law returns to the lower house for final approval.
